## Natural history notes

A small flea beetle characterized by its compact oval body, enlarged hind legs for jumping, and dark body often marked with pale or reddish-orange striping or patches. In Florida, it is found on low vegetation in fields, roadsides, pine flatwoods, forest edges, prairies, and other open or semi-open habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults feed on leaves and jump quickly when disturbed, while the larvae develop on or near host plants; one reliable host record is St. Andrew’s-cross, though other reported host associations may need confirmation.
